coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Schedule Wayback/own-snapshot capture of hrc.si, halcom.com, printecgroup.com and payten.com reference pages and diff quarterly.

coverage_gaps.description: No Slovene-language podcast, newsletter or video-commentary source was identified for banking and payments, though such formats increasingly carry off-record executive commentary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted searches for 'podkast bančništvo Slovenija', 'newsletter finance Slovenija', and check Finance.si / Svet kapitala / Forbes Slovenija for podcast verticals; also check YouTube channels of the major outlets.

coverage_gaps.description: No historical media archive route was established for reconstructing fee or ATM-network changes before roughly 2015; paywalled dailies do not expose deep archives publicly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate the Digital Library of Slovenia (dLib.si) and COBISS for digitised runs of Finance, Delo and Bančni vestnik, and check whether Slovenian outlets are covered by any press-archive aggregator.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language commentary specifically on the Slovenian payments market is thin and mostly from non-Slovene vendors (The Fintech Times, GlobalData, TheBanks.eu, sloveniabusiness.eu), which lag and simplify the Slovene reporting.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Do not rely on English sources for this cell beyond STA English and the November English issue of Bančni vestnik; treat English vendor reports as leads to be re-verified in Slovene.

coverage_gaps.description: Merchant- and acquirer-side media commentary (retail trade press, hospitality associations complaining about POS acceptance costs) was not covered by this cell's searches.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Slovene trade press for 'trgovci provizije kartično plačilo', 'Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije plačilne kartice', and the hospitality sector, to capture the merchant view of interchange and POS fees.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice are search-derived; none were fetched and none should be treated as liveness-verified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass; treat 403/timeout as bot-defence (likely live) and only 404/NXDOMAIN as evidence of a moved or dead source.

coverage_gaps.description: The only genuinely SI-specific instrument-level market sizing (GlobalData, ResearchAndMarkets yearbook, Argus Advisory) is entirely behind commercial paywalls; only abstracts and press releases are harvestable.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Budget for one edition of the GlobalData or Argus Slovenia report to anchor the series, and otherwise systematically harvest free abstracts and vendor press releases each cycle.

coverage_gaps.description: Nothing in this cell produced independent ATM/POS terminal-estimate series or cash-logistics analysis; the aggregators reference POS/ATM counts only inside paywalled products, and no consultancy paper on SI cash infrastructure was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rely on the regulator/official-statistics cells for ATM/POS counts and use this cell only for forecasts and attitudinal colour; explicitly cross-check any aggregator ATM/POS figure against Banka Slovenije.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian-language consultancy output is thin: apart from Deloitte SI's DBM article and EY SI's insights feed, the Big Four publish about Slovenia mainly in English regional reports. Local-language depth comes instead from academia (RUL, CEK) and survey/media relays.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Weight academic repositories and SI media relays more heavily for sl-language coverage of this cell rather than expecting sl consultancy reports.

coverage_gaps.description: Global research houses likely to hold SI cuts were not individually confirmed this pass: Capgemini World Payments Report, Roland Berger, Oliver Wyman, Kearney European Retail Banking Radar, and Euromonitor/Mintel consumer-finance data.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass on these five aggregators specifically querying Slovenia country coverage before declaring the cell complete.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian survey houses beyond Valicon (Mediana, Ninamedia, Aragon, Parsifal) were not individually searched, and none was confirmed to run a payments-specific tracker.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Second pass in Slovenian on 'agencija za raziskavo trga' + 'plačila'/'banke' to enumerate the national survey-house landscape.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level adjudication touching Slovenia (European Commission competition decisions, CJEU/Curia rulings on interchange and payment accounts, EBA consumer-trends and payment-fraud reports) was not systematically covered in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up sweep of curia.europa.eu, EC DG COMP case register and EBA publications filtered for Slovenian parties or SI-specific data.

coverage_gaps.description: No verification pass was made on AVK's decision-archive pagination depth or on whether older interchange/banking cases sit only in the pre-2013 Urad za varstvo konkurence (UVK) archive under a different domain or naming.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl the full odločbe archive index including legacy UVK-era records; search alias terms 'Urad RS za varstvo konkurence', 'UVK'.

coverage_gaps.description: Complaint and dispute data specific to ATM/POS access and card acceptance (as opposed to accounts and credit) is thin; no source found that breaks complaints down by card/ATM/POS category.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Parse ZBS IRPS opinion PDFs case-by-case to build a home-made category taxonomy (card fraud, ATM withdrawal, fee dispute) and derive counts.

coverage_gaps.description: Second-tier consumer bodies were not explored: Mednarodni inštitut za potrošniške raziskave (MIPOR, ZPS research arm), Zveza potrošnikov' European Consumer Centre Slovenia (ECC-Net SI), and the Ministry of Economy consumer-protection directorate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sl-language sweep on MIPOR, Evropski potrošniški center Slovenija and MGTŠ varstvo potrošnikov for cross-border payment complaint statistics.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all entries rest on search-result evidence only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass before any URL is treated as reachable, and re-resolve the two root-level URLs (varuh-rs.si annual reports index, gov.si TIRS) which were inferred from result context.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial-bank careers pages are covered only for Deželna banka and (indirectly) NLB. NLB, OTP banka (ex Nova KBM), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, SKB (OTP Group), Addiko, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica and Sparkasse careers pages and their LinkedIn hiring feeds were not reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one sl query per issuer ('<bank> kariera zaposlitev placilne kartice / placilni promet') and register each careers URL; add LinkedIn company pages as manual-review sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-usage weak signals (CIT companies, cash-in-transit and ATM-estate operators, independent ATM deployers, Bankart's ATM outsourcing partners) were not searched at all. Job ads and tenders from CIT/ATM service firms are the clearest early indicator of ATM estate contraction or expansion.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sl terms: 'prevoz gotovine', 'oskrba bankomatov', 'servis bankomatov zaposlitev', 'vzdrzevanje POS terminalov razpis'.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement / tender portals (e-JN, portal javnih narocil) were not covered in this cell. Bank and public-sector tenders for POS terminals, ATM servicing and payment software are a strong pre-announcement signal, and award notices disclose volumes and values.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ejn.gov.si / Portal javnih narocil keyword monitoring, and coordinate with whichever cell owns procurement so it is not double-covered.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage in this slice is thin — only one en query completed successfully (the awards query) plus the BSI Fintech Hub en page. The en-language regional event circuit (payments conferences in AT/HR/RS with Slovenian speakers) is unexplored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Next pass, run en queries on 'Slovenia payments conference speakers', 'CEE payments summit Slovenia Bankart NLB speaker', and EPCA/EAST ATM-industry membership pages.

coverage_gaps.description: No systematic snapshot inventory was built. The Wayback CDX API was identified as the method but not executed, so it is unknown which SI payment-statistics pages are already well-archived and which are at risk of loss.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a CDX enumeration over bsi.si/statistika*, bsi.si/placila-in-infrastruktura*, bankart.si and each bank domain; proactively Save-Page-Now every live statistics page in the run's target list.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell supplies denominators only. Actual payment, card, ATM and POS transaction counts for Slovenia are published by Banka Slovenije and the ECB, which fall outside this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Ensure the Banka Slovenije / ECB payment-statistics cell is scouted, and define the join keys (period, NACE where available) so SURS denominators and central-bank numerators can be aligned.

coverage_gaps.description: Eurostat re-publishes the Slovenian ICT household/enterprise survey, HBS and national accounts in harmonised form with a stable bulk-download API, which was not explored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout Eurostat dataset codes (isoc_ec_*, isoc_e_*, nama_10_co3_p3, hbs_*) as an alternative, more automatable access path with cross-country comparability.

coverage_gaps.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live by this agent; all URLs come from search-result evidence and cross-references between sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over all example_urls, treating any 403 as bot-defence rather than death and re-checking stat.si DocSysFile PDF ids, which are opaque and prone to rotation.

coverage_gaps.description: SURS retail turnover and ICT indicators are national and, at best, cohesion-region level; no municipality-level or merchant-category-level breakdown suitable for terminal-density modelling was identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Combine the AJPES PRS business register (entity-level, with addresses and SKD codes) with SURS structural business statistics to synthesise sub-national merchant density rather than expecting SURS to publish it.

coverage_gaps.description: The household budget survey (APG) runs only every few years while payment statistics are monthly or quarterly, and the COICOP 1999 to COICOP 2018 switch introduces a break in the consumption series.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Anchor high-frequency normalisation on monthly retail turnover and quarterly national accounts, and use APG only for structural basket weights; explicitly record the COICOP break date in the series metadata.

coverage_gaps.description: No SKD/NACE activity-code sweep was performed to build the candidate list of Slovenian ATM servicing, POS terminal supply and payment-technology companies from the business register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the relevant SKD codes (e.g. 62.0x IT services, 33.12/33.20 repair and installation of machinery, 46.51/46.66 wholesale of computers and other office machinery, 66.19 other auxiliary financial activities) and run them against the OPSI PRS bulk CSV to generate a candidate actor list, then triage by name and filed accounts.

coverage_gaps.description: Card acquiring in Slovenia is largely performed by banks and by the domestic processor, so no acquirer-specific list was located; scheme-side sources (Visa/Mastercard licensed acquirer and principal-member lists for SI) were not searched in this slice.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted pass on card scheme licensee/principal member listings and on Banka Slovenije card statistics publications to enumerate acquirers, then reconcile against the credit-institution register.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact machine-readable interfaces for AJPES (ePRS reuse service, OPSI resource endpoints) and for EBA EUCLID were not read in detail; only their existence and general terms were established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the AJPES 'Ponovna uporaba' page and the OPSI resource metadata to capture download URLs, refresh cadence and licence text; confirm the EUCLID public API endpoint and its rate limits before designing the pipeline.

coverage_gaps.description: JOLP is described as giving access to recent years online, with older years obtainable only at AJPES offices; the precise online retention window was not confirmed, and eObjave documents are retained online for only one year.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm the JOLP online retention window and start archiving eObjave documents immediately for watchlist entities, since the one-year window means history is irrecoverably lost if collection starts late.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian-language coverage was strong for AJPES and Banka Slovenije, but no Slovenian-language terms were available or used for the supranational EBA/EUCLID sources, which are English-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept English-only for EU-level registers; no Slovenian equivalent exists. Continue prioritising SL terminology for all national sources.

coverage_gaps.description: State-owned / public-interest entities that plausibly tender ATM, POS, cash-handling or core-banking services were not individually investigated: Pošta Slovenije (postal counters and cash), SID banka, SDH (Slovenski državni holding), UJP (Uprava RS za javna plačila), DARS (tolling POS/payment acceptance), Slovenske železnice, and large municipalities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass enumerating these authorities by name against enarocanje.si, TED (buyer name), ERAR and DKOM decisions; each is a distinct contracting-authority node.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified CPV code set for ATM/cash dispensers, card issuing/personalisation, and core banking software.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Retrieve the official CPV nomenclature (SIMAP/TED) and pin the exact code ranges for divisions 30 (office/computing machines), 48 (software incl. banking systems), 66 (financial services) and 79 (security services), then encode them as the harvest filter.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language glossary is solid for cash transport and ATMs but thin for card issuing/personalisation and core banking. Terms such as 'personalizacija plačilnih kartic', 'izdajanje kartic', 'jedrni bančni sistem', 'core banking sistem', 'kartično poslovanje' were used only partially; noisy terms identified: 'bankomati' (dominated by bank ATM-locator pages), 'razpis' (also means scholarship/donation calls), 'javni razpis' (grants, not procurement).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the sl glossary with card-issuing and core-banking vocabulary and re-run portal-internal searches; explicitly separate 'javno naročilo' (procurement) from 'javni razpis' (grant call) in query design.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian national open data starts at 2013 (Evidenca javnih naročil); pre-2013 national coverage was not established, though TED FTP reportedly reaches back to 1993.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use TED bulk XML for the pre-2013 window and document the discontinuity in any longitudinal series.

coverage_gaps.description: Automated access characteristics (robots.txt, rate limits, JS-rendering, ToS) were not tested for enarocanje.si, ejn.gov.si, erar.si or dkom.si.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a technical feasibility probe on each before designing collectors; prefer OPSI/TED structured endpoints wherever they duplicate portal content.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice come from search-result metadata; none were fetched and confirmed reachable in this pass, and several deep PDF paths (year-foldered NLB, ISP, OTP downloadfile ids) are of the kind that rotate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every candidate; on 404 re-derive from the issuer index page rather than marking dead, and on 403/timeout retry with browser-like headers.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank sustainability/ESG reports, Pillar 3 disclosures beyond Gorenjska banka and Sparkasse, and AJPES JOLP (public filed annual accounts) were not systematically searched, though AJPES is the statutory repository where every Slovenian bank files.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass on AJPES JOLP for filed annual reports of all licensed banks and savings banks, plus each bank's razkritja/Pillar 3 page; both give comparable structured filings independent of issuer web design.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign-bank branches and niche private issuers in Slovenia (e.g. BKS Bank AG branch, N Banka wind-down legacy, Deželna banka Slovenije, UniCredit Banka Slovenija) were not covered in this pass; DBS and UniCredit in particular are material card/ATM issuers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map from the Banka Slovenije register subjektov nadzora and the ZBS member list, then run the same letno-porocilo/bankomati/kartice query template against each missing actor.

coverage_gaps.description: Branch/ATM locator pages were classified as indirect sources on reasoning, but their backing data endpoints, robots.txt posture and record counts were not inspected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Reconnaissance task: for nlb.si, otpbanka.si, intesasanpaolobank.si and dh.si locators, identify the JSON/map API, count records, and check robots.txt/ToS to establish whether periodic counting is permissible.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale assumes private banks bypass public procurement portals, but bank-to-vendor relationships for ATM hardware, card personalisation and processing (e.g. Bankart as the shared national processor) are not visible in the sources gathered here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Handle in a processor/vendor-focused cell: annual reports name shared infrastructure providers, and those providers' own disclosures can reveal fleet and card volumes the banks omit.

coverage_gaps.description: National Payments Council minutes (38 sessions, 2014–2026) and the 'Strategija razvoja plačilnega trga v Sloveniji 2024–2028' were identified but not read in this pass; only one minutes PDF URL was captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate and bulk-download all approved NSP session minutes from bsi.si (storage/uploads paths) plus the 2024–2028 strategy, then extract per-organisation statements to attribute association positions on fees, cash access and instant payments.

coverage_gaps.description: Bančni vestnik full texts (1952–2026) are partly login-gated; the free subset was not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the 'Brezplačni članki' subset and the free English special issues; harvest metadata for the whole archive; assess subscription cost for full-text access to payments/cards articles.

coverage_gaps.description: TZS member area and its T-Informacije bulletin, and OZS member advisories, are unindexed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Evaluate paid membership or a direct information request to TZS and OZS for their payments/NSP briefings; meanwhile mine public news pages and NSP minutes for merchant-side statements.

coverage_gaps.description: Združenje Povezani smo was identified only through media coverage; its own website/domain was not located, so its primary materials (petition text, submissions) are uncaptured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Targeted sl search for the association's own domain and its parliamentary submissions (DZ RS record) on the cash constitutional amendment; downgrade or drop if no primary source exists.

coverage_gaps.description: ZBS's memberships in supranational bodies (e.g. European Banking Federation, ESBG/WSBI, EPC) were not confirmed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check EBF/ESBG/EPC national-member directories for the ZBS entry — those profiles often carry SI country factsheets with payment and branch/ATM figures in English, filling the EN-language gap for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovensko zavarovalno združenje (Slovenian Insurance Association) is an NSP member but was not profiled; likewise the e-commerce/online-retail association layer was not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile Slovensko zavarovalno združenje for its payments-related interests, and run sl queries for a Slovenian e-commerce/online-retail association (spletna trgovina, e-poslovanje) covering card-not-present acceptance.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language association output was thin: only ZBS (EN annual reports, EN site, Bančni vestnik English special issues) and TZS (/en landing) offered EN material; GZS PTZ, OZS, ZPS and the NSP minutes are effectively Slovenian-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan machine translation of sl-only association corpora (NSP minutes, ZBS press releases, ZPS reviews) rather than expecting EN equivalents; do not use EN-only querying for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Per-acquirer tariff/price lists ('cenik', 'tarifa') of SI banks acting as acquirers (NLB, OTP, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Deželna banka, SKB/OTP) were not individually located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sweep for '<bank> cenik POS terminal provizija trgovec' and 'tarifa za kartično poslovanje' per acquiring bank; these PDFs are the only public MDR evidence in SI.

coverage_gaps.description: Bankart's recent annual reports and any published statistics/newsroom feed were not enumerated from the site itself (only via search).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl bankart.si sitemap.xml and /wp-content/uploads/ year directories directly to enumerate all published PDFs; also check for a 'novice'/news section and press contacts.

coverage_gaps.description: Visa's Slovenian-language presence (visa.si / visa.com sl-si) was not checked for SI-specific interchange or press pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search and fetch visa.si and visa.com/sl-si equivalents of the Mastercard SI interchange page to complete scheme-side local-language coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Independent ATM operators / white-label ATM deployers and cash-in-transit players in SI (relevant to cash usage and ATM data) were not covered in this cell's pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a targeted sweep for 'neodvisni upravljavci bankomatov Slovenija', Euronet SI presence, and BSI's list of ATM-operating entities.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovenian Competition Protection Agency (AVK) and EU Commission antitrust files on card interchange were not searched.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sweep varstvo-konkurence.si (AVK) and EC competition case register for card-scheme/interchange decisions touching Slovenia; these often disclose market shares and fee levels.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice were obtained from search results or a single fetch and are unverified for liveness by design.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic verification pass resolve status codes; treat 403/timeout as bot-defence rather than dead.

coverage_gaps.description: The Banka Slovenije register of licensed payment institutions, e-money institutions and account information service providers, and the EBA central credit-institution/payment-institution register, were referenced in secondary sources but not directly located and pinned to a URL in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Directly navigate bsi.si to the supervision/register section ('register plačilnih institucij', 'družbe za izdajo elektronskega denarja', 'ponudniki storitev zagotavljanja informacij o računih') and pin the register URLs and any downloadable exports; do the same for the EBA credit institutions register filtered on SI.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic acquiring/POS and A2A-adjacent actors were not searched in this pass: Halcom (corporate e-banking and payment software), Petrol Pay / Petrol's QR ecosystem, Nexi/Worldline activity in SI, Rekono (identity provider used for wallet onboarding), and small-bank Flik participants such as Delavska hranilnica and Gorenjska banka.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second sweep with queries such as 'Halcom takojšnja plačila', 'Petrol Pay QR plačilo statistika', 'Rekono identiteta plačila', 'Delavska hranilnica Flik' to complete the actor map for the A2A/wallet rail.

coverage_gaps.description: The ECB SPACE study (Study on the Payment Attitudes of Consumers in the Euro area) and any Banka Slovenije consumer payment-habits survey were not searched, yet these are the canonical bridge between instant/wallet adoption and cash usage at point of sale.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search for 'ECB SPACE study Slovenia' and 'Banka Slovenije raziskava plačilnih navad potrošnikov' and add the national SPACE country annex as a candidate; it is the main source linking this cell to the cash-usage topic.

coverage_gaps.description: SURS (Statistični urad RS) and its SiStat database were not queried for ICT/e-commerce usage indicators (share of individuals using mobile payments, internet banking penetration), which provide independent adoption denominators.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query SURS/SiStat for 'uporaba interneta bančništvo mobilna plačila' indicators and add the SiStat API/dataset as a candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement portals (e-JN / Portal javnih naročil) and Diavgeia-equivalent transparency channels were not searched. Tenders for instant-payment, wallet or e-invoicing infrastructure reveal spend, vendors and roadmap ahead of any press release.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a sweep of the Slovenian public procurement portal for keywords 'plačilni sistem', 'takojšnja plačila', 'e-račun', 'mobilna denarnica' and register it as a recurring indirect source.

coverage_gaps.description: Several candidate URLs were assembled from actor knowledge rather than confirmed in a search result: the EPC SCT Inst register export path, the Wero/EPI domains, the ZBS Bančni vestnik e-archive root, the Valú product page and the AJPES eRacuni deep link.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Route these through the deterministic liveness pass and replace any that redirect; treat them as unverified until then. None were fetched in this pass, so no liveness claim is made for any URL in this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial market reports (GlobalData 'Slovenia Cards and Payments to 2028', Statista card-purchase series) surfaced but were not assessed for licensing or value.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide policy on paid syndicated research; if in scope, record GlobalData and Statista as licensed sources with cost and redistribution constraints rather than collecting them.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash recycling and automated cash deposit infrastructure in Slovenia is entirely uncovered - no terminology, vendors, bank deployments or central bank accreditation lists were identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated Slovenian-language pass on 'vplacilni bankomat', 'depozitni bankomat', 'bankomat z vplacilom gotovine', 'recikliranje gotovine', 'denarni center'; check Banka Slovenije's cash pages for any register of accredited cash handlers under the Eurosystem framework for banknote recirculation; and check hardware vendor country pages (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, GRG, Sigma/CIMA distributors) for Slovenian references.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM withdrawal volumes and values, and any geographic breakdown of cash withdrawal activity, were not located in national sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the ECB Data Portal payment statistics for Slovenia (ATM withdrawal number and value series) and the Banka Slovenije statistical data series files directly rather than relying on the press summaries; also check the annual ECB SPACE study for Slovenian payment-behaviour shares of cash at point of sale.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM hardware, software and managed-services vendors serving the Slovenian estate were not investigated at all in this pass - only deployers, banks and CIT firms were mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Slovenian public procurement (portal javnih narocil / e-narocanje) for bank and municipal ATM tenders to identify supplying vendors and contract values, and check regional distributor and integrator sites. Bank tenders are a reliable route to vendor identity and estate refresh cycles.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement records were identified as the likely richest untapped source for both municipal ATM subsidies and bank ATM/CIT contracts, but were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically query the Slovenian public procurement portal for 'bankomat', 'prevoz gotovine', 'varovanje in prevoz gotovine' to extract contracting authorities, winning bidders, contract values and durations - the only public route to per-ATM and per-route cost data.

coverage_gaps.description: The individual written responses to the ZDUPS public consultation (closed 17 August 2026) were not retrieved - only third-party reporting on ZBS's and OZS's positions.

briefs: Banka Slovenije is unambiguously the primary creator and mandated publisher of Slovenian payment, card, ATM/POS and cash statistics, compiling them under ECB Regulation 1409/2013 (ECB/2013/43) as amended by ECB/2020/59 and nationally under Sklep o poročanju podatkov statistike plačil (Ur. l. RS 108/2021). The cell has a clear three-layer structure: a machine-readable semi-annual data layer in the PxWeb warehouse (folder serije_slo__10_denar_mfi__95_spi, ~28 live tables plus ~10 pre-2022 archive tables covering cards by function and scheme, issuer- and acquirer-side card payments by channel and SCA method, resident- and non-resident-provided terminals, ATM cash withdrawals and deposits, credit transfers, direct debits and e-money); a narrative layer of press releases, the annual Poročilo o plačilnih in poravnalnih sistemih and the recurring bank-fee comparison publication; and a definitional/regulatory layer of reporting instructions, CRD/ACC templates, code lists and the Register subjektov nadzora. Access is open and free with no bot-blocking observed, and the main risks are structural rather than legal: the 2022 ECB/2020/59 reporting change splits the series into two non-identical table sets, bsi.si serves two coexisting URL path families that will generate duplicates and spurious 404s, headline cash-in-circulation is an ECB capital-key allocation rather than a national count, and nothing below national aggregate is published — so any per-bank or per-acquirer ATM/POS estate sizing must be sourced from operator, processor or bank-report cells instead.

For Slovenia, the EU/ECB layer is the strongest and most automatable part of the payments evidence base: the ECB Data Portal (successor to the SDW) carries SI as a country row in the PSS, PTT, PCP and BKN dataflows, all reachable through a documented SDMX 2.1 REST API at data-api.ecb.europa.eu with semi-annual publication (H1 by end-January, H2 by end-July). On cash, the ECB SPACE consumer study and the companion company cash survey (SUCH) are the only rigorous, cross-country measurements of cash use at the point of sale — Slovenia consistently ranks near the top of the euro area (64% of POS payments by number in the 2024 wave) — but both are PDF-only, so extraction rather than API access is required. Regulatory and structural sources complete the cell: the EBA PSD2 Payment Institutions Register and Credit Institutions Register give a downloadable, diffable population of Slovenian PSPs and banks, the annual EBA–ECB payment fraud report gives country-level fraud benchmarks, and the Commission/ERPB/ECA policy layer signals what changes next. Slovenian-language material is essentially absent at this level, so sl-language monitoring for this cell has to route through Banka Slovenije's relays of ECB studies.

The Slovenian merchant/POS-side landscape has one unusually strong public asset: FURS fiscal-verification open data on podatki.gov.si, which reports the daily count and value of every fiscally verified invoice at 5-digit SKD level — but which, by legal design, folds card payments into 'cash payment' and therefore cannot itself yield a cash-vs-card split. Merchant-level payment mix is disclosed only anecdotally through the press (Petrol ~50% cash, Mercator somewhat under 60% cash), so the workable method is to combine FURS till volumes with Banka Slovenije acceptance statistics (~47,000 POS terminals at end-2024, +11% y/y) and with retailer disclosures via Mercator/SEOnet, Petrol IR and AJPES filings for the unlisted foreign-owned chains (Spar, Hofer, Lidl). The vendor layer is domestic and fragmented — Mikropis/MikroPOS (Mercator Tik-Tak self-checkouts, exports to Korea/China), Microgramm, POS Elektronček, Krajnik as hardware distributor, plus fiscal-software houses (Birokrat, MetaKocka, Minimax, Vasco) — with no official register of ECR software producers, so the vendor map must be built bottom-up. Acceptance economics at the long tail are being actively reshaped by the Visa/bank/GZS 'Slovenija plačuje digitalno' subsidised-terminal programme, which is both a tracked intervention and an admission of how thin card acceptance still is among micro and small SI merchants.

The vendor/supplier indirect route is unusually productive for Slovenia because the market's technology supply is concentrated and the suppliers advertise loudly. Two anchors dominate: HRC d.o.o. (Hibis), a domestic core-banking vendor that publicly names essentially the whole second tier of SI banks and savings banks and claims >50% market share, and Bankart, the shared processor whose supplier choices (Diebold Nixdorf Vynamic replacing Base24; Nets/Nexi RealTime24/7 behind instant payments) are disclosed in vendor and IR press releases with estate scope and country counts. Around them sit ATM/self-service and terminal players (Printec/NCR, Diebold Nixdorf, Euronet as independent deployer, Payten/ASEE), Temenos at NLB, and Halcom whose e-banking pages publish rare volume proxies and a bank-coverage roster. Main weaknesses of this cell in this pass: no card-personalisation or cash-logistics vendor route was established, no Slovenia-specific Nexi/Worldline acquiring announcement was found, kontron-slovenia.com was unreadable due to a TLS chain error (unverified, not dead), and the session's search budget ran out before Payten-SI and Flik-supplier queries could run.

Slovenia's banking and payments media landscape is small, concentrated and overwhelmingly Slovene-language: three tiers matter — the paywalled business press (Finance.si, Delo/Svet kapitala, Forbes Slovenija) which carries fee, market-share and profitability detail; the free public-interest layer (RTVSLO, STA wire and its republishers Siol.net and N1) which is the reliable, archivable record of Banka Slovenije statements, instant-payments/Flik developments, ATM-density legislation and cash-access policy; and a specialist/indirect layer (Bančni vestnik from the bank association, ZPS consumer tests, Cekin.si comparison hubs, Slo-Tech forum threads) that generates or first surfaces the numbers the press later amplifies. The most operationally valuable non-obvious finds are Necenzurirano.si for payment-outage and core-system-failure investigations, entity tag pages across delo.si/siol.net/cekin.si as durable free pointer feeds behind the paywalls, and Bančni vestnik as the only sustained specialist analysis venue including an annual English issue. Two structural cautions: 'kartično poslovanje' and similar Slovene terms collide with Croatian/Bosnian coverage and must be domain- or actor-anchored, and no standalone Slovene fintech commentary blog of the type the cell brief anticipated could be found — that function is dispersed across the outlets above.

For Slovenia, the aggregator/consultancy landscape splits into three tiers. Foreign commercial research houses (GlobalData, ResearchAndMarkets, Argus Advisory, Statista) hold the only genuinely SI-specific cards-and-payments sizing and forecast series — instrument-level volumes, issuer/scheme shares, cash share above 40% of volume — but almost all of it sits behind paywalls, leaving only abstracts and press releases freely harvestable. Among the Big Four, only Deloitte produces reliable Slovenia-specific output (Digital Banking Maturity, CE Banking Outlook, CEE M&A Banking Study, plus a Slovenian-language DBM write-up); PwC, EY and KPMG SI offer publication indexes worth monitoring but no confirmed SI banking or payments study. Attitudinal data on cash versus cards comes almost entirely from Mastercard's Masterindex survey, released through scattered SI media rather than a stable page, with no Visa counterpart found — a single-sponsor dependency worth flagging. Slovenian-language depth is supplied instead by academia: the RUL and CEK repositories carry full-text theses reproducing SI card, POS and interchange tables, and SICRIS/COBISS provides a systematic pointer into every SI researcher and project in the field.

Slovenia's non-central-bank regulatory and consumer-protection layer is fragmented but unusually rich in fee-level evidence. The highest-value quantitative assets are the statutory Banka Slovenije fee-comparison series and the ZPS comparator (bank-by-bank pricing for accounts, cards and ATM withdrawals), backed by ZBS's IRPS out-of-court dispute opinions and caseload counts, which are the only public complaints statistics found for banking. AVK contributes market-structure evidence through merger decisions and its odločbe archive rather than through interchange enforcement — no national interchange decision was found, which is itself a finding. The most consequential live thread is the legislative one: the new constitutional right to use cash (art. 74.a) and the draft ZDUPS with hard ATM-coverage and free-basic-package obligations, whose consultation file on gov.si carries industry cost submissions unavailable anywhere else.

Slovenia's weak-signal layer for banking-payments is small but unusually concentrated: Bankart, as the national card/ATM/POS/SEPA processor, is the single richest node — its own job ads, versioned Flik integration PDFs, LinkedIn feed and third-party-mirrored recruitment decks together disclose stack, roadmap and volume claims well ahead of formal announcements. Event agendas are the second pillar, with Delo DPC's 'Mobilne tehnologije' conference the most payments-specific (2026 edition puts Banka Slovenije, NLB payments/cards and Bankart on one programme), backed by ZBS's training catalogue and recorded banking conference, and DSI's per-year programme subdomains which double as an archive. Hiring signals are best harvested from the statutory ESS vacancy register plus Optius/Zaposlitev.net and the central bank's own vacancy pages; awards, by contrast, appear to be a genuinely empty sub-channel in Slovenia. Recovery of superseded data rests on Banka Slovenije's own /arhiv and National Payments Council e-newsletter paths plus systematic Wayback CDX enumeration, neither of which has yet been inventoried — that, issuer-bank careers pages, and cash-in-transit/ATM-servicing hiring are the main open gaps.

Slovenia's denominator layer for payments intelligence is unusually well-consolidated: SURS publishes everything through one PxWeb database (SiStat) with a documented REST API in PX/CSV/JSON-stat, mirrored dataset-by-dataset on the national open data portal OPSI, and scheduled in advance via a public release calendar — so this cell can be collected deterministically rather than scraped. The highest-value series are monthly retail turnover, national-accounts household final consumption by COICOP, and the annual EU-harmonised ICT household survey, the last of which uniquely reports how online purchases were paid for (card versus cash on delivery versus bank transfer) and is therefore the only SURS-side direct read on card-versus-cash behaviour. Beyond SURS, AJPES supplies the statutory entity and financial-statement layer — its business register is open bulk XML, but JOLP annual reports are gated behind registration and a hard 20-subjects-per-day cap that forbids bulk collection — while FURS's real-time receipt fiscalisation captures cash-versus-card at transaction level but appears not to publish aggregates. The cell's hard boundary is that SURS produces no payment, card, ATM or POS transaction counts and no recurring account-ownership indicator; those must come from Banka Slovenije, the ECB, or Eurostat mirrors, which should be scouted separately and joined to these denominators.

Slovenia's register landscape for payments is unusually clean at the licensed end and unusually thin at the hardware end. Banka Slovenije operates a single filterable Register subjektov nadzora covering roughly 372 entities across 14+ supervisory categories — banks, payment institutions, e-money issuers, AISPs, payment system operators, exchange dealers — backed by dedicated PI and EMI registers, EEA passporting lists and dated notification PDFs; AJPES then supplies the identity and money layer via the freely reusable Poslovni register Slovenije (bulk CSV on the OPSI open-data portal), the eObjave court-register gazette for corporate events, and JOLP for filed annual accounts including banks and insurers. Together these turn the licensed market into a named, joinable list with revenue proxies per actor, with EBA EUCLID as an independent cross-check. The material gap is that independent ATM deployers and POS/terminal operators are not licensed or registered anywhere as such, so that population must be constructed by SKD-activity sweeps over the business register and snowballed from press and company self-disclosure; two practical constraints to plan around are JOLP's 20-subjects-per-day cap and the one-year online retention of eObjave documents.

Slovenia has an unusually well-instrumented procurement transparency stack for this cell: the statutory notice portal (enarocanje.si) and its transaction system (e-JN) are mirrored into machine-readable OPSI datasets covering notices, awarded contracts and even published contract texts from 2013 onward, with TED providing the above-threshold, CPV-coded, API-accessible EU layer back to the 1990s. Three high-value secondary layers turn notices into hard intelligence: ERAR (KPK) shows realised payments to named suppliers including e-invoices since Sep 2024, DKOM decisions expose tender specifications and bidder disputes in detail, and the Court of Audit flags off-portal or non-compliant spend. The principal structural limit is that Slovenia's commercial banks are not contracting authorities, so this channel captures public-sector and state-owned demand for ATM, POS, cash-in-transit and core-banking services rather than the whole national fleet — a scoping caveat that must be carried into any sizing estimate. Priority next steps are pinning the exact CPV code set for ATM/card/core-banking categories and enumerating named contracting authorities (Pošta Slovenije, UJP, SID banka, DARS, large municipalities) rather than relying on keyword search, since general web engines do not index individual Slovenian notice pages.

For Slovenia's private banks the disclosure landscape is bimodal: two listed issuers (NLB on LJSE/LSE, Addiko Bank AG on Vienna) publish rich, quarterly, English-language investor material with explicit network, card and ATM-fee commentary, while everyone else — OTP banka (the merged Nova KBM + SKB), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank, Gorenjska banka, Delavska hranilnica, Sparkasse, LON, Primorska hranilnica — discloses only through Slovenian-language letno porocilo PDFs on their own sites, typically with a 'poslovna mreza' section carrying branch, ATM and card figures. Local-language querying was essential: 'letno porocilo', 'poslovna mreza', 'bankomati', 'karticno poslovanje' and 'javne objave' surfaced the PDF archives that English queries never returned. Two structural cautions dominate: the 22 August 2024 Nova KBM/SKB merger breaks every network and card time series and puts the skb.si archive at risk of retirement, and no bank in this cell publishes machine-readable network data, so collection means scheduled PDF extraction plus branch/ATM locator scraping as an independent cross-check. Nothing in this slice was fetch-verified — every URL is a search-derived candidate awaiting the deterministic liveness pass.

Slovenia's bank/PSP association layer is dominated by one node — Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS-GIZ) — which is rich as a pointer and position source (member directory covering banks, savings banks and a separate leasing tier; 2001–2025 annual reports in SL and EN; a press archive carrying explicit sector positions on cash accessibility, instant payments and the digital euro; national payment standards such as UPN QR, ISO 20022 and the payment-purpose code register; and the Bančni vestnik journal archived back to 1952) but does NOT publish aggregated payment, card, ATM or POS statistics — its data page is chart images sourced from Banka Slovenije. The genuine cross-industry aggregation point is instead the Nacionalni svet za plačila (National Payments Council), whose 22 members map the entire SI payments actor set (ZBS, TZS, GZS, ZPS, Bankart, Nexi Slovenija, Dinit, Petrol Pay, Telekom Slovenije, Odbor za shemo Flik, Visa, Mastercard, plus ministries and agencies) and whose 38 published session minutes plus the 2024–2028 payment-market strategy are the highest-value uncollected corpus in this cell. The merchant/acceptance side (TZS, GZS Podjetniško-trgovska zbornica, OZS) is present but its payments material is largely member-gated, and no dedicated Slovenian association for non-bank PSPs or fintechs appears to exist; the consumer counterweight is ZPS, whose bi-monthly cross-bank fee comparator is the only regularly refreshed non-central-bank pricing aggregation. Cash policy is a live and unusually hard constraint here: bank-sector statements on cash accessibility now sit against a constitutionally entrenched right to pay in cash driven by the advocacy association Združenje Povezani smo.

Slovenia's card ecosystem has an unusually concentrated data core: Bankart d.o.o., the bank-owned domestic switch and processor, both creates the transaction data and discloses scale figures on its site and in its annual reports, while Banka Slovenije publishes the national denominators (cards, ATMs, POS terminals) and describes the Poravnava kartic settlement system Bankart operates. Scheme-side, the useful public material is pricing rather than volume: Mastercard's Slovenian-language 'medfranšizne stopnje' disclosure, Visa Europe's country interchange tables, and Worldline's Slovenia scheme-fee PDF; neither scheme publishes SI transaction volumes, so those must come from the ECB PCP dataset and BSI. Legacy brands remain live but transformed — Activa, created in 1992 at Banka Koper, is operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo and survives as Activa Mastercard products, while Diners Club Slovenija is now issued by Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. The main open gaps are per-acquirer merchant tariffs (the only public MDR evidence in SI), Bankart's post-2020 annual reports, and independent ATM operators.

Slovenia's instant/A2A landscape is structurally very well documented but poorly quantified in public: Banka Slovenije (payment instrument statistics, National Payments Council minutes, annual report) and the ECB Data Portal supply the authoritative aggregate series, while Bankart — operator of BIPS, the TIPS link, Flik, the Flik Pay gateway, the interbank e-invoice exchange and the national PSD2 HUB — is the single richest operator-side node and the natural centre of any collection design. The critical asymmetry for this cell is that Flik itself publishes no recurring statistics: every user, volume and value figure in circulation (roughly 776k–800k users, ~1.5–2m transactions monthly, a ~EUR 126m peak month, ~90% still P2P) reaches the public only through operator statements relayed by ZBS articles and Slovenian media, so a provenance-tagged press-citation series is unavoidable and must never be presented as official data. Wallet-side coverage is best tracked through structured vendor censuses (Apple's participating-banks list, Google Wallet's equivalent) diffed over time, plus per-bank product pages and the non-bank wallets mBills and Valú; the open-banking and e-invoicing legs are enumerable (Bankart HUB ASPSP list, per-bank statutory API disclosures, UJP's daily recipient register) but carry no published volume data. Priority follow-ups are the BSI/EBA licence registers, the ECB SPACE consumer study for the cash-substitution link, and recent Bankart annual reports via AJPES filings.

Slovenia's ATM and cash-access source landscape is unusually rich right now because a constitutional right to use cash (Article 74a) is being implemented through the draft Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (ZDUPS), whose July-August 2026 public consultation has forced Banka Slovenije, the bank association ZBS, municipalities and merchants to argue with numbers in public. The estate itself is exceptionally observable: Banka Slovenije semi-annual payment statistics give the authoritative counts (around 1,284-1,304 ATMs, a 30 percent decline since 2011, 61.1 per 100,000 inhabitants), while the Bankart PSD2 open-banking hub and its rendered front-end ATMinfo.si expose near-real-time per-bank ATM locations, counts and uptime - making address-level closure tracking technically feasible. The cash logistics leg is mapped through regulation rather than commerce: the MNZ private-security licence register on the national open data portal yields the complete legal population of CIT operators (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT, IBS), which joined to AJPES accounts allows the segment to be sized, with no global CIT major evident beyond G4S. The principal blind spots are withdrawal volumes, cash recycling infrastructure (for which no Slovenian terminology or actor could be established), and the unretrieved ZDUPS consultation filings and municipal ATM procurement records, which are the likeliest repositories of otherwise unpublished coverage and cost data.
